Let's be honest, Voat is Reddit targeting a different demographic. There's less bullshit here - people speak their minds. As a result of this and our anti-hivemind mentality, when disagreement occurs, it's bigger and more public. Voat is growing and finding its feat; there are teething problems at the moment because different people want different things from the community. One of the largest challenges is that we're all very much pro-free-speech, but the community largely wants to deny a platform to those who are anti-free-speech (e.g. SJWs and their ilk). There is hypocrisy in that, but IMO it's a necessary hypocrisy. Lots of people have become very paranoid recently that we're being infiltrated. It's almost certainly the case that we are being infiltrated, but the problem is that some people see enemies in every shadow. It's a very Orwellian experience and quiet enlightening to be part of.
